footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. From pre-tax income to net income to common: after income tax and $5.4M of preferred dividends & other. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose 19.6% to $325M in 2025. Net interest income rose 20.1% to $273M and noninterest income rose 16.6% to $51.5M; noninterest expense rose 14.3%, and the provision for credit losses was $11.3M, versus $10.9M.
Net income to common rose 38.1% to $82.5M, or $2.79 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 62.5% versus 65.4%. Business First Bancshares returned $20.6M through dividends and buybacks.
highlights: Net income to common rose 38.1% to $82.5M.
watch: Net interest income depends on interest rates.
